Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

solid adjective

also solid (not hollow), solid (not liquid), solid food, solidify, set (go solid), sturdy, solidly built

classical

Cic. Top. 22: pariēs vel solidus vel fornicātus (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Div. 1.48: a solid gold column, against a gilded one (Lewis & Short)

solidus, solida, solidum

solid: dense, not hollow; firm

Solid through and through, against hollow, gilded or liquid: aurō solidī, of solid gold (Verg. A. 2.765); in solidum coīre, to set solid. It also means whole and entire (see whole).

Other words

  • firmus, firma, firmum — firm, sturdy, strong

    also used · classical · Lewis & Short, s.v. firmus: firm in opposition to frail

    Solid as strong and stable: a table, a wall, a friendship.

Examples

  • nam etiam maximum solida nōn recēpērunt, rūrsus ārida et corripī facilia scintillam quoque fovent ūsque in incendium

    for solid logs won’t take even a great flame, while dry stuff that catches easily nurses even a spark into a blazeSen. Ep. 18.15

  • perque coāgula dēnsa liquor in solidum coit

    and with thick rennet the liquid sets solidPrud. Cath. 3.66–70

See also whole, hard, liquid, gold.
